generator: HelioSI paper-to-skill factory (HelioSI paper-to-skill factory, Opus 4.7) — waves/instabilities/reconnection/kinetic batch (corpus_step_to_500)

harness_framing.principle: Paper-skills are harness-agnostic. LingTai, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenAI Assistants are adapter examples, not assumptions in the skill body.
skill_layers: 2. Scientific invariant layer (claims, equations, methods, data assumptions, failure modes, figure targets)
3. Executable protocol layer with abstract capability contracts (C-*)
harness_framing.research_generation_affordance: Every SKILL.md includes a §5 Research-generation affordance with at least one tension/gap/open-hypothesis seed; many also link composable sibling skills via [[slug]] edges. This is the load-bearing element that turns the corpus from a static catalog into a hypothesis-generation substrate.

compilation_framing.model: Each paper is compiled from arXiv/ADS abstract + theme-inventory record into a runtime-neutral paper-skill describing capability contracts and scientific invariants. Most entries are STUB-tier with explicit TODO_verify_with_full_text tokens and an executable_status of contract-spec-only-not-yet-runnable.
compilation_framing.stub_policy: Stub allowed per HelioSI project requirement; TODOs explicitly marked in DOI/arxiv fields, numerical targets, and §2.5 reproduction targets so a future full-text pass can convert stub → paper-grounded-pending-full-text → paper-grounded-locally-reproduced.

claim_boundaries.scope: 45 new paper-skills covering waves, instabilities, reconnection, kinetic plasma physics, and dissipation in heliophysics, harness-agnostic and additive to the 96-skill corpus baseline.
out_of_scope: No skill in this batch is full-text-verified or end-to-end runnable.
All capability-contract names (C-*) are abstract; no MCP or library is asserted as a dependency.
Source attribution is via the theme_wave_analysis.json inventory record; DOIs, arXiv IDs, author lists are marked TODO_verify_with_full_text where the inventory is incomplete.
Research-generation affordances (§5) are seeds, not a publication-ready research agenda.
